item.title: Legitimacy of Labor Market Policy: Public Attitudes Towards Welfare State Responsibility for Job Creation
item.description: This article tests a number of hypotheses for explaining the effects of personal and contextual characteristics on attitudes towards the government’s role in job creation. item.title: Students’ Perspectives on Family Values in Bosnia and Herzegovina: At the Crossroads Between Tradition and Modernity
item.description: This study explores changes in family values and orientations among students in Bosnia and Herzegovina, with a focus on their perceptions of traditional and modern family models. item.title: Exploring the Gender Dynamics in the Rice Value Chain Interventions in Nigeria
item.description: This study, conducted in Taraba, Kebbi, Kwara, Ebonyi, Akwa-Ibom, and Ekiti states, Nigeria, explored the structure of the rice value chain (RVC) and gender dynamics therein using a qualitative methodology. Data was collected through in-depth interviews (IDI) and focus group discussions (FGDs) and analyzed using content analysis. The study was grounded in the framework of African feminism. item.title: Practicing Sociology: The Role of Theory in Applied Research
item.description: The article argues that a degree in sociology provides an academic qualification rather than a professional qualification, and hence sociology cannot be practiced. item.title: Report on the 3rd ISSP User Conference “Celebrating 40 Years of the International Social Survey Programme"
item.description: The International Social Survey Programme (ISSP) Secretariat and the editors of the planned special issue of the International Journal of Sociology (IJS) organized an online conference on the anniversary edition of the ISSP User Conference on 25 November 2024. Stephanie Steinmetz opened the conference with a short welcome and introduction to the ISSP.

item.title: Personal Enrichment vs Social Welfare: The Impact of Public Procurement in South Africa
item.description: The South African Constitution allows preferential procurement to reverse historical economic segregation. item.title: The Suburbanisation of Social Exclusion: Examples from Czechia

item.title: Employee Perceptions of the Contributory Pension Scheme and Its Implications for Job Satisfaction in the Nigerian Public Service
item.description: This qualitative phenomenological study investigates employees’ experiences regarding the influence of the contributory pension system on job satisfaction in the Nigerian public service. item.title: Social Entrepreneurship Ecosystems in Bulgaria: Levels, Key Actors, Success Factors and Social and Environmental Impact
item.description: Social entrepreneurship ecosystems can address society’s wicked problems more rapidly and on a larger scale than a single social enterprise working alone.
